mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2.5% year-over-year signals inflationary pressures that typically lead to tighter monetary policy, which in turn increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.5% does not correlate with subsequent tightening cycles.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points in one month signals a weakening labor market, which typically precedes a broader economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE rise does not correlate with subsequent economic slowdowns.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in Real Final Sales (RSAFS) over two consecutive months signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenues and earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or RSAFS decline does not correlate with subsequent earnings reductions.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in Industrial Production (INDPRO) by more than 2% month-over-month signals a surge in economic activity, which typically leads to increased corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or INDPRO surge does not correlate with subsequent earnings growth.

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 4% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) is increasing, the combination signals a tightening monetary policy in the face of inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the interaction of FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL does not correlate with subsequent tightening cycles.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in Nonfarm Payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 300,000 in a month signals strong labor market conditions, which typically leads to increased consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or PAYEMS increase does not correlate with subsequent consumer spending growth.

mechanism_narrative: When Housing Starts (HOUST) decline by more than 10% month-over-month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) rises by more than 0.3 percentage points, the combination signals a weakening economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST declines > 10% MoM and UNRATE rises > 0.3pp
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the interaction of HOUST and UNRATE does not correlate with subsequent economic contractions.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a strong economic expansion, which typically leads to increased corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of instances despite the positive signal, or GDPC1 increase does not correlate with subsequent earnings growth.
